text: [Frank & Freedus v. Allstate Ins. Co., supra, 45 CA4th at 471-472, 52 CR2d at 684] • [3:402] Employee claimed he had been sexually harassed by Supervisor. Employer's President gave a radio interview regarding Employee's claims. During the interview, President acknowledged that Supervisor had AIDS. Supervisor (whose job had been eliminated) sued President for defamation and invasion of privacy. Supervisor's claims were not covered under Employer's liability insurance. The “employment-related practices” exclusion applied because the only relationship between President and Supervisor was an employment relationship. [Low v. Golden Eagle Ins. Co. (2002) 104 CA4th 306, 316, 128 CR2d 423, 430] [3:403 - 3:404] Reserved. 3) [3:405] Reconciliation of views? One court has attempted to reconcile these interpretations as follows: The fact the alleged tort arose after the employment relationship ceased does not itself remove the claim from the scope of the employment-related practices exclusion.
